MAMMON — Money Acquisition, Monetisation & Making-Ends-Meet Operations Network — v0.1
PRIVATE CLOUD9 / EDEN DEVELOPMENT HANDOFF
Owner: Lucas Buzek
Status: Experimental / Private
Purpose: Continue MAMMON development in a new chat without redesigning established canon.

STARTING INSTRUCTION
Continue MAMMON from this handoff. Do not restart product design. Preserve established EDEN authorities, identities, privacy boundaries, provenance and unresolved historical canon. Apply:
IMPLEMENT / INTEGRATE EXISTING CAPABILITY BEFORE RECREATING IT.
MAXIMUM USEFUL MODULARITY — MINIMUM DUPLICATION.
MANY APPS, ONE AUTHORITY PER CAPABILITY, MINIMAL DUPLICATION.
DETERMINISTIC BY DEFAULT; INTELLIGENCE ON DEMAND.
EVERY UNKNOWN SHOULD BECOME A QUESTION, A SEARCH, OR A DELEGATION — NEVER AN INVENTION.

1. PRODUCT IDENTITY
MAMMON is a small independent private EDEN App focused on personal/family income-generation campaigns and economic opportunity strategy.
Expanded satirical name:
Money Acquisition, Monetisation & Making-Ends-Meet Operations Network.
Concept/tagline:
“MAMMON doesn’t manage your money. It helps you go get some.”

MAMMON is NOT:
- HERMES replacement.
- MONETA replacement.
- accounting authority.
- generic job board.
- generic research engine.
- autonomous authority for consequential commitments.

MAMMON owns:
- income-generation campaign strategy;
- opportunity intelligence synthesis;
- monetisation hypotheses;
- cross-domain opportunity matching;
- economic strategy around opportunities;
- strategic experiments and feedback from outcomes.

2. USER-FACING WORKSPACE
HEIMDALL Workspace: MAKE MONEY.
MAMMON is the App/strategy authority behind this private Workspace.
Possible satirical private UI language established:
Coffers; Hunt; Schemes; Tribute Due; Grind; Probably Not Worth It; Graveyard; Loot.

3. PRIVACY / AUDIENCE
Private cloud9 capability only for Lucas, his wife and explicitly authorized family members.
Do not treat MAMMON/MAKE MONEY as a public or default Family & Friends feature.
Keep identities, permissions and financial/opportunity data separated.
Shared family views/data are explicit opt-in.
Consequential submissions, contracts, purchases, bids, commitments or irreversible external actions require appropriate user approval.

4. CORE MISSION
Continuously observe the world, detect potentially monetizable change, model the opportunity, challenge the hypothesis, determine actionable strategy, execute through appropriate EDEN Apps, and measure whether it actually produced money.

Potential signals include:
- emerging markets and technologies;
- trends;
- social-media virality/statistics;
- news and breaking events;
- world/geopolitical events;
- jobs, freelance, contracts and tenders;
- business/procurement opportunities;
- products, services and content opportunities;
- search trends;
- cultural movements;
- communities/forums;
- industry changes;
- shortages/demand;
- new APIs/software/providers;
- regulatory changes;
- geography-specific needs;
- EDEN capability reuse opportunities.
Rumour/gossip/social signals are low-confidence leads, not facts, and must be verified before being treated as evidence.

5. AUTHORITY MAP / INTEGRATIONS
MAMMON — strategy/campaign intelligence and monetisation.
HERMES — authoritative jobs/opportunities, applications, bids/engagement records and opportunity pursuit.
MONETA — authoritative financial semantics/state: budgets, costs, pricing, cash flow, profitability, invoices/payments, tax/treasury/reporting as applicable.
ARGOS — research, evidence quality, verification, opposition/red-team and synthesis.
THREAD — historical context, provenance and recovery of prior project material.
CONDUCTOR — intent interpretation, decomposition, orchestration and capability/provider resolution.
BIFROST — interoperability, discovery, provider connections, routing, events and transport abstraction.
HEIMDALL — MAKE MONEY Workspace composition/presentation/configuration.
CASPER — larger/general writing and documentation.
SKALD — writing within its established narrower purpose.
LINGUA — translation/localization.
FORGE — implementation/build/test/package/release.
WEAVER — web implementation.
GrandMasterRegister + Capability Manifests — canonical identity, authority, capability and provider contracts.

BRIDGED ≠ DEPENDENT. Apps remain independently useful and degrade gracefully.

6. MAMMON STRATEGIC PIPELINE
High-level opportunity cycle:
DISCOVER → VERIFY → MODEL → STRATEGIZE → RESPOND → WIN → PLAN → EXECUTE → ADAPT → VALIDATE → DELIVER → INVOICE → COLLECT → LEARN

For a concrete task offer:
1. INGEST original offer, source, client, deadline, compensation, requirements, attachments and communications.
2. VERIFY with ARGOS: legitimacy, scam indicators, contradictions, unknowns and evidence quality.
3. DECOMPOSE with CONDUCTOR: requirements → deliverables → acceptance criteria → dependencies → capabilities → resources → deadlines.
4. CAPABILITY MATCH through EDEN; BIFROST resolves providers.
5. ECONOMICS through MONETA: compensation minus costs, fees, external services, compute/API costs, labour/time and other relevant inputs.
6. RESPONSE via HERMES plus appropriate writing capability; commitments require user approval.
7. Build executable workflow graph with ordered/parallel tasks, checkpoints, QA, client preview/revisions, delivery, invoice/payment and outcome analysis.
8. Dynamically replan around blockers, missing inputs, provider failure, scope changes and effort overruns.

Canonical rule:
WORKFLOW STEPS ARE CAPABILITY REQUESTS, NOT JUST TEXT IN A TO-DO LIST.

7. OPPORTUNITY MODEL
Each opportunity should be representable with:
- Signal
- Evidence
- Confidence
- Timing window
- Domain/market/geography
- Actors
- Competition
- Lucas/family capability match
- Required resources
- Missing capabilities
- Candidate providers
- Initial cost
- Time requirement
- Potential return
- Downside/risk
- Dependencies
- Alternative strategies
- Information gaps
- Next cheapest experiment
- Stop / continue / pivot conditions
- Actual outcome

Track estimated vs actual effort/return, conversion, revenue, margin, payment delay, failures and provider performance.

8. CROSS-DOMAIN OPPORTUNITY DISCOVERY
EDEN must not be restricted to humanitarian/community applications. MAMMON should search for legitimate value across domains.

Application domains currently identified include:
Humanitarian & Development; Agriculture & Food; Environment & Conservation; Water; Energy; Housing & Construction; Manufacturing & Industry; Transport & Logistics; Healthcare & Biomedical; Education & Research; Communications & Connectivity; Computing & AI; Media & Creative Industries; Commerce & Entrepreneurship; Finance & Economic Development; Tourism & Hospitality; Government & Civic Infrastructure; Emergency & Disaster Response; Security & Resilience; Defence-support & Peacekeeping; Geopolitics & Strategic Intelligence; Space & Remote Exploration; Marine Systems; Mining & Resources; Household/Personal Technology.

Do NOT automatically create one App per domain. Use:
EDEN capability → domain application → opportunity → Workspace/project → existing Apps/Specialists → execution.

Opportunity Matrix dimensions:
DOMAIN × GEOGRAPHY × PROBLEM × CUSTOMER × TECHNOLOGY × TREND × REGULATION × EVENT × AVAILABLE CAPABILITY × RESOURCE × TIMING

Bidirectional search:
A. Capability → where else can this create value or income?
B. Problem/opportunity → what existing EDEN capabilities can solve it?

9. SWEATSHOP — TASK EXECUTION WORKERS
SWEATSHOP is the intentionally satirical private/internal name for a pool of NON-HUMAN software task workers/agents. Formal documentation may use “Task Execution Workers.”
It is not a human-labour concept.

Purpose:
Take bounded objectives/work packages from MAMMON/CONDUCTOR and execute persistently within explicit capability, data, permission, budget, deadline, resource and stop-condition constraints.

Workers should be:
- specialized;
- cheap/ephemeral where practical;
- parallelizable;
- observable;
- cancellable;
- replaceable;
- disposable after completion;
- capable of deterministic execution as well as AI-assisted execution.

Workers may use deterministic scripts/tools, existing EDEN Apps/Specialists, local/LAN/online AI, native applications, external services and repositories through authorized BIFROST providers.

Worker lifecycle:
SPAWN → RECEIVE OBJECTIVE → EXECUTE → REPORT → VALIDATE → DELIVER ARTIFACT → TERMINATE

Blocked:
BLOCKED → REFRAME → ALTERNATE PROVIDER → ESCALATE TO CONDUCTOR/USER

Execution Contract:
- Objective
- Inputs
- Expected output
- Allowed capabilities
- Allowed data
- Provider policy
- Budget
- Deadline
- Resource ceiling
- Validation criteria
- Escalation conditions
- Stop conditions

A worker need not be an LLM. It may be a script, CLI process, existing App automation, native AI, local/LAN/online model, Specialist delegation or provider workflow.

Private satirical UI terms proposed:
Open the Sweatshop = active workers
Hire = spawn
Fire = terminate
Overtime = resource allocation
Foreman = CONDUCTOR orchestration
Assembly Line = workflow graph
Output = artifacts
Productivity = execution metrics
Wages = compute/API/provider cost
Strike = blocked workers

Canonical relationship:
MAMMON finds the opportunity.
CONDUCTOR devises/orchestrates the strategy.
SWEATSHOP supplies task-specific digital workers for execution.
EDEN Specialists provide expertise.
MONETA determines whether it was worth doing.

10. SWEATSHOP RESEARCH / LOCAL MODEL OPTIMIZATION LOOP
SWEATSHOP output is also empirical optimization data, subject to privacy/rights controls.

Capture where permitted:
- objective/task class;
- inputs or privacy-safe descriptors;
- chosen capability/provider/model;
- prompts/instructions/templates where applicable;
- tool calls;
- deterministic steps;
- latency;
- resource/API cost;
- retries;
- failures/blockers;
- validation results;
- human corrections/acceptance;
- final outcome;
- downstream economic result.

ARGOS analyzes the corpus to find:
- repeatable task patterns;
- failure modes;
- unnecessary AI usage;
- prompt/context inefficiencies;
- deterministic substitutions;
- provider/model strengths;
- tasks suitable for local-model specialization.

Optimization order:
1. remove unnecessary AI calls;
2. improve task decomposition;
3. improve context/retrieval;
4. improve prompts/contracts/tools;
5. improve provider routing;
6. optimize local inference/model/quantization/caching/batching/hardware use;
7. only then consider fine-tuning/distillation/specialization.

Keep separate:
Execution Log
Research Corpus
Evaluation Corpus
Training Corpus

Private/client/family data does NOT automatically become training data.
Training/distillation/fine-tuning data must be curated, deduplicated, provenance-tracked, quality-scored, privacy-filtered and rights/consent checked.
Maintain holdout/evaluation sets.
Benchmark quality, latency, memory/compute, energy and cost.
Promote model/config changes only on measured improvement without unacceptable regressions.

Closed loop:
EXECUTE → CAPTURE → VERIFY → RESEARCH/OPPOSE → CLASSIFY → OPTIMIZE → BENCHMARK → PROMOTE/REJECT → ROUTE BETTER → EXECUTE

11. GENERALS / ROGUES STRATEGIC PROVIDERS
Do NOT invent a new generic strategist roster where existing project assets already exist.

Existing strategic bodies:
A. Modern Generals — Generals roster.
B. Rogues Gallery.

Use them as strategy/personality providers through EDEN/BIFROST while preserving their own project identities and provenance.

Strategic War Room concept:
GENERALS — competing strategic doctrines and approaches.
ROGUES — unconventional/asymmetric angles and overlooked paths.
ARGOS — verifies evidence and attacks assumptions.
MAMMON — converts surviving strategies into economic scenarios.
CONDUCTOR — turns scenario into executable strategy/capability graph.
SWEATSHOP — executes bounded work.

Pipeline:
INTELLIGENCE → GENERALS → ROGUES → ARGOS OPPOSITION → GAME THEORY/SIMULATION → MAMMON → CONDUCTOR → SWEATSHOP → RESULTS → ARGOS ANALYSIS → LOCAL MODEL OPTIMIZATION

12. MODERN GENERALS / GAME-THEORY INSPIRATION
Reuse strategic mechanics as modelling inspiration, NOT as factual economic truth.

Useful mappings:
market/environment = map
actors/competitors = players
skills/capabilities = available units
equipment/software = assets
new capabilities = tech tree
market/customer access = territory/access
capital/cash flow = resources/resource generation
time = strategic pressure
unknowns = fog of war
dependencies/logistics = supply lines
build cost = investment
income = resource generation
expansion = market/capability expansion
counter-strategy = competitor/adversarial response
win condition = objective
retreat = stop/pivot

Previously identified Modern Generals strategic research themes include economy/income generation, production flow, resource expansion, AI priorities, grouping, retaliation, supply safety and behavior-based AI rather than crude stat inflation.

Keep fictional/game data strictly separated from real-world evidence and financial truth.

13. GENERALS GENERATIONS — IMPORTANT CANON
Generals “Generations” are NOT technology tiers or upgrade levels.
They represent multiple conceptual/doctrinal evolutions in how gameplay describes combat, strategy and geopolitical dynamics.

The established direction includes movement from narrower conventional-force framing toward broader systems thinking: resources, logistics, infrastructure, information, alliances, economics, legitimacy, technological dependence, population needs, resilience, influence, adaptation, regeneration, distributed capability and long-term outcomes.

Earlier EDEN Generals material recovered in current context includes:
Architect, Gardener, Shepherd, Voyager, Guardian, Falconer and Tinkerer.
A documented strategic cycle was:
SEED → GENERATE → FABRICATE → ADAPT → RECLAIM → EXPAND → RELOCATE

CRITICAL:
The exact historical multi-generation sequence/names/order have NOT yet been reliably recovered.
Treat them as UNRESOLVED HISTORICAL CANON.
Use THREAD/source recovery to reconstruct the original lineage.
DO NOT manufacture “Generation 1/2/3…” replacements.
When recovered, expose the Generals generations as reusable strategic lenses for Modern Generals, MAMMON, AEGIS, ARGOS, CONDUCTOR and simulation/decision Workspaces while preserving provenance.

14. ROGUE / ROGUES GALLERY
ROGUE was discussed as the archetype that asks:
“What is the clever route everyone else missed?”
However, the existing Rogues Gallery/roster must take precedence over creating duplicate permanent strategist identities.

Potential rogue-like functional lenses discussed:
SCOUT — obscure sources/emerging opportunities.
THIEF — satirical label for extracting maximum LEGITIMATE value from open/authorized resources via reuse, repurpose, arbitrage and salvage; never theft.
INFILTRATOR — difficult ecosystems, integrations, legacy/platform constraints via authorized means.
TRICKSTER — unconventional combinations.
SMUGGLER — legitimate movement/conversion/export/import between awkward systems.
LOCKPICK — compatibility/integration blockers through supported/authorized interfaces.
FENCE — legitimate channels for monetizing/licensing/publishing/marketplace assets.
PICKPOCKET — tiny efficiencies/savings/revenue opportunities.
GRIFTER — defensive study of scams/hype/manipulation.

Boundary:
ROGUE may break assumptions, conventions and inefficient workflows — not authorization, law, consent or system boundaries.

Do not duplicate these as permanent specialists if the existing Rogues Gallery already covers them.

15. AEGIS / MILITARY-GEOPOLITICAL APPLICATION BRANCH
A new EDEN application branch was proposed:
AEGIS — Applied Engineering, Geopolitical Intelligence & Security.

This is ONE branch among many, not the total non-humanitarian expansion.

Purpose:
Protect people, infrastructure, information and essential capability under difficult or contested conditions.

Focus areas:
- geopolitical intelligence/scenario analysis;
- critical-infrastructure resilience;
- field engineering/logistics;
- communications/distributed/off-grid computing;
- situational awareness and defensive security;
- recovery/continuity planning.

Potential practical applications:
portable solar/microgrids, water monitoring, emergency communications, LoRa telemetry, offline maps/knowledge, equipment/inventory tracking, logistics optimization, infrastructure fault detection, environmental sensing, search-and-rescue support, disaster assessment, cyber-defensive monitoring, portable servers, resilient agriculture, field repair systems, evacuation/logistics planning and infrastructure restoration.

Intelligence cycle:
OBSERVE → SOURCE → VERIFY → CONTEXTUALIZE → COMPARE HYPOTHESES → RED TEAM → ASSESS CONFIDENCE → MODEL SCENARIOS → IDENTIFY PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCES → PLAN RESILIENCE

Engineering emphasis:
protection, sensing, communications, logistics, resilience, recovery and decision support.
Military/geopolitical research and doctrine may be studied, but EDEN engineering output should remain oriented toward legitimate protective/resilience/support applications rather than systems whose primary function is harming people.

17. DETERMINISTIC + AI EXECUTION
Target pattern:
USER INTENT → AI INTERPRETATION → STRUCTURED PLAN → DETERMINISTIC RESOLUTION → EXECUTION → DETERMINISTIC VALIDATION

Unknown handling:
deterministic attempt → identify unresolved variables → normalize/reframe → retry → resolve provider → provider assistance → deterministic validation → execute or present unresolved choice

AI is appropriate for ambiguity, semantic interpretation, novel planning, research, code/content and semantic merges.
Deterministic systems should own registry/IDs, capability matching, compatibility, dependencies, policy filters, permissions, builds, testing, packaging, formal sync/routing rules and measurable validation where possible.

18. PROVIDER / DEVICE MODEL
MAMMON/SWEATSHOP must request capabilities, not hard-code model/provider names.
BIFROST/CONDUCTOR resolve providers from:
native OS capabilities;
installed applications;
application-native AI;
EDEN components;
local/LAN AI nodes;
scripts/CLI/workflows;
self-hosted services;
online/cloud/API providers;
repositories/package sources.

Every capable device can be client and provider.
Routing should consider task fit, privacy, authorization, availability, cost, latency, resource use and quality.
Discovery never equals authorization.

19. ECONOMIC LEARNING
MAMMON must learn from actual outcomes, initially through deterministic statistics/configuration rather than assuming model retraining.

Feedback:
Signal → hypothesis → decision → action → cost/time → result → revenue/margin → assumption review

Measure:
- opportunity category;
- predicted vs actual effort;
- predicted vs actual return;
- conversion;
- revenue;
- margin;
- payment delay;
- failures;
- provider performance;
- worker/model/tool cost.

20. HISTORICAL INCOME CONTEXT TO RETAIN
Prior income-support work included:
- target of at least US$200/week remote income;
- technical/creative service opportunities;
- biomedical/engineering/renewable-energy documentation;
- consulting;
- photo/video/multimedia;
- web/content work;
- opportunity scoring by pay, fit, ease, automation, competition, recurring potential and effective $/hour after automation;
- useful categories: high-value specialist, creative, simple/automatable and recurring;
- labels previously proposed: HIGH PAY, FAST CASH, AUTOMATABLE, RECURRING, SA ACCESSIBLE.
These can inform MAMMON but should not constrain it to freelancing.

→ ARGOS post-analysis
→ local-model/provider optimization evidence

Acceptance test:
A legitimate opportunity is discovered or supplied, evaluated, converted into an executable workflow, completed using real EDEN capabilities/providers, economically measured, and fed back into the research/optimization loop.
